- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in 10-30 day horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase low-range forecasts, especially for 10-15 day horizon.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., 1.00 → 0.00 → 1.00), leading to overcorrection; apply lagged smoothing or dampen 3-5 day spikes.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10-15 day horizon; if forecast is >2.5σ above recent mean, reduce by 15-25% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates tail risk (e.g., >10.0) when sentiment is mixed or negative; cap forecasts at 1.5x recent 18-day average unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- If sentiment history shows 3+ consecutive 0.00 values, model underperforms; increase forecast by 10-20% for 10-15 day horizon to compensate for low sentiment bias.
